article: Post Slack messages with a bot OAuth token from C++
scope: Compared the Japanese source and all twelve translations, current Slack token and chat.postMessage behavior, scopes, channel membership, JSON encoding, WinHTTP resource cleanup, response handling, metadata, and links.
findings: Clarified that OAuth code exchange is not implemented.
Moved the bot token to an environment variable and required a channel ID.
Added JSON escaping, RAII handle cleanup, and HTTP plus Slack ok checks.
Removed the incorrect token-type table and added current primary references.
Preserved the 2025 publication date and added lastmod.

post/Slack App + OAuth2 を使って Slack にメッセー.source: post/Slack App + OAuth2 を使って Slack にメッセージを投稿する方法/index.md
post/Slack App + OAuth2 を使って Slack にメッセー.summary: Compared the full translation with the Japanese source and updated token setup/security, scopes, channel permissions, WinHTTP request/response handling, metadata, and references.

meaning.note: Clarified that the sample uses an installed app bot token and does not implement OAuth authorization-code exchange.

terminology.note: Reviewed Slack bot token, OAuth scope, bearer auth, channel ID, UTF-8 JSON, WinHTTP, and security wording.

mathematics.note: The article contains no mathematical claims or formulas.

code.note: Replaced raw JSON concatenation and token literals with escaping, environment loading, RAII handles, HTTP status and Slack JSON ok checks. Static review only; not compiled or sent to Slack.

links.note: Added current Slack chat.postMessage/token docs and Microsoft WinHTTP API references; checked localized internal links.

limitations: AI-assisted review by Codex; no human or native-speaker certification.
The C++ sample was reviewed statically but not compiled or sent to a Slack workspace.
The small response helper checks the top-level ok boolean; production clients should use a JSON parser and robust diagnostics, timeout, and retry handling.
The example assumes an installed app with permissions; it does not implement OAuth consent, callback handling, or token refresh.
Use a secure secret store for production tokens.
